thread:
olivia: incident-bot paged: latency_slo_breach for pool shared-gpu-pool-7, p95 420ms (SLO 200ms), p99 1.8s (SLO 500ms). streaming stalls increasing across multiple tenants.
oncall-bot: @olivia you are now on-call for incidents. ack required. :rotating_light:
cheng: acked. pulling metrics and active tenants now. seeing a sudden IO wait spike on node gpunode-17.
marta: confirmed, customer-ops-bot shows 3 tenants with >50% error-rate on streaming sessions: acme-inc-prod, beta-vision, demo-team.
ryan: any recent deploys? I don't see a staging rollout in last 6h.
cheng: no deploys. kernel iostats show high avg await on nvme1 (reads 12ms -> 80ms). cgroup blkio.throttle.io_serviced shows elevated counts for tenant cgroup ids: 1203, 1314.
olivia: probable noisy neighbor on shared pool. priority: mitigate customer impact and then root cause. Plan: 1) quick tenant isolation (move acme-inc-prod to reserved fallback pool) 2) throttle offending tenant or adjust cgroup limits 3) monitor p95/p99 and streaming stall metrics.
marta: can we live-migrate acme-inc? use the routing fallback to dedicated-evictable-1?
cheng: yes, we can route traffic at the controller layer. command: `curl -X POST "https://controller/api/v1/route/move" -d '{"tenant":"acme-inc-prod","dest":"reserved-fallback-03"}'`
ryan: if we migrate, sessions will need reconnect, streaming clients might see brief stalls. we should warn customer-ops and set expectations.
olivia: customer-ops-bot, prep a message for Acme with ETA ~3m for migration and potential 10-30s client disconnect.
customer-ops-bot: Draft message to acme-inc: "We detected increased latency on your streaming sessions and are migrating you to an isolated pool to restore performance. You may experience a brief disconnect (~10-30s). We'll confirm when done." Approve?
marta: approve. send.
cheng: starting migration now. hitting controller API... response 202. moving active sessions is streaming-aware, will replay KV cache where possible.

dry-run logs:
```
INFO routing.move requested tenant=acme-inc-prod dest=reserved-fallback-03
INFO sync: draining current workers for tenant acme-inc-prod
WARN kvcache: partial miss for session 9012, replay in progress
INFO attach: 7 streams reattached to new worker
```

ryan: monitoring latency graph — p95 for acme-inc drops from 420ms -> 190ms after reattach. p99 still at ~480ms for a minute. error-rate dropping.
olivia: good. now we need to identify offending tenant(s) causing IO pressure. who are the top cgroup users?
cheng: top offenders by blkio time: tenant 1314 (beta-vision) performing large read bursts from dataset shard s3://vision-bench causing sustained NVMe reads. tenant 1203 (demo-team) doing frequent small synchronous writes. both contributing to queue depth.
marta: can we temporarily throttle beta-vision reads at the kernel cgroup layer? e.g., set blkio.throttle.read_bps_device for nvme1 to limit.
cheng: applying soft throttle now: `echo "8:0 100000000" > /sys/fs/cgroup/blkio/tenant-1314/blkio.throttle.read_bps_device` — applied.
ryan: after throttle, node iowait drops, p95 across pool falls to ~220ms, p99 ~540ms. streaming stall logs show fewer retry loops.
olivia: good interim. next: long-term followups — recommend: move heavy batch datasets to dedicated pools, implement per-tenant IO quotas at admission, add an automated noisy-neighbor detector that raises a ticket when blkio dev await above threshold for 2 consecutive minutes.
cheng: creating a follow-up issue: https://issues.redwood/INFR-4923 — notes attached (blkio graph, top processes, tenant IDs).
marta: also need a postmortem and customer impact assessment. acme-inc saw 2.3 p95 spike minutes, 14 sessions with reconnects; beta-vision had degraded throughput but not outage.
olivia: action items assigned: Cheng -> investigate disk pattern and recommend kernel tunables + cgroup policies; Ryan -> run bench on reserved-fallback-03 to confirm capacity and add route fallback test to synthetic suite; Marta -> draft postmortem + customer email; Olivia -> update runbook with migration play and noisy-neighbor checklist.
sre-runbook-bot: Runbook step executed: tenant-migration succeeded, mark incident as mitigated if all affected tenants p95 < SLO for 10m.
cheng: metrics now steady for 12m: pool p95 185ms, p99 420ms.
marta: recording timeline and tagging slack thread in postmortem doc.
olivia: closing on-call handoff in 10m. final customer note sent to acme-inc and ops confirmed.
ryan: one last note — consider exposing per-tenant IO metrics in console as a first-class metric (blkio await, read_bps). will add to roadmap ticket.
olivia: thanks team. I'm un-acking. :thumbsup: If anything regresses, re-open the thread.
oncall-bot: oncall cleared: olivia -> none.
